BACONC P'UP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. S. 2021 DOLORES S. CAULIS Attorney-in-Fact 9008 Ronquilio St., Kanaway, Sta. Cruz, Cavite City Dear Ms. Cajulis. This has reference to your letter dated 05 June 2024 seeking the Department's Legal Opinion regarding the enforcement of the Paranaque City Local Committee Against Professional Squatters and Squatting Syndicates (LCAPSSS) Resolution No. 2024-01 dated February 7, 2024 against the families identified as professional squatters and squatting syndicates in Kawayanan, Moonwalk. Per the representation, the LCAPSSS of Paranaque City resolved in the abovementioned Resolution granting an order to summarily eject the illegal occupants/settlers occupying the Kawayanan Compound in accordance with law and due process. However, you represented that the LCAPSSS of Paranaque City was not implementing the abovementioned Resolution and you are reminding the Local Government Unit of Paranaque regarding the mandate of LGUs provided under Section 27 of R.A. 7279, otherwise known as the "Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992". Also, you represented that you have exhausted all administrative remedies provided by law and the Constitution to ensure that the rights of families to be evicted are not violated. You also mentioned that you are willing to have dialogues with the affected families to provide humanitarian and financial assistance. Thus, the request for legal opinion on what measures should be taken to on how the subject resolution of LCAPSSS Paranaque will be enforced by the LGU of Paranaque to address the issue of professional squatters in the Kawayanan property. At the onset, Section 27 of R.A. 7279 clearly provides that LGUs have the mandate to identify and effectively curtail illegal activities of professional squatters and squatting syndicates, viz: "Sec. 27. Action Against Professional Squatters and Squatting Syndicates. — The local qovernment units, in cooperation with the Philippine National Police, the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP), and the PCUP accredited urban poor organization in the area, shall adopt measures to identify and effectively curtail the nefarious and illeqal activities of professional squatters and squattinq syndicates. as herein defined. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Any person or qroup identified as such shall be summarily evicted and their dwellinqs or structures demolished, and shall be disqualified to avail of the benefits of the Program. A public official who tolerates or abets the commission of the abovementioned acts shall be dealt with in accordance with existinq laws. For purposes of this Act, professional squatters or members of squatting syndicates shall be imposed the penalty of six (6) years imprisonment of a fine of not less than Sixty thousand pesos (P60,000.OO) but not more than One hundred thousand pesos (PI 00,000), or both, at the discretion of the court." (Emphasis supplied) Also, DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2012- 04, specifically provides the power of LCAPSSS, through the Local Chief Executive as chairman, to curtail the activities of professional squatters, to wit: "Powers and Functions (2.2.2 of Executive Order No. 129; Section 9 (b), Chapter II, Implementing Guidelines of Executive Order No. 153) I. Adopt the necessary measures to identify and effectively curtail the activities of professional squatters and squattinq syndicates in order to safeguard against their inclusion in future government housing programs/projects and recommend their disqualifications in existing programs; Xxxx" (Emphasis ours) From the foregoing, LGUs, through their respective LCAPSSS have the responsibility to effectively curtail the nefarious and illegal activities of professional squatters and squatting syndicates. Thus, it can be stated that the LGU of Paranaque City, through their LCAPSSS, has a duty to implement the subject Resolution by evicting the illegal occupants/settlers occupying the Kawayanan Compound in line with the law and due process requirements. Considering their mandate to implement the Resolution, failure of the Local Chief Executive, as chairman of LCAPSSS, or its members to eject the illegal occupants and settlers occupying the Kawayanan Compound may result to gross negligence or dereliction of duty under Sections 60 (c)l of the Local Government Code, or under the 2017 Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service (2017 RACCS) for appointive officials. As a result, you may immediately request that the LCAPSSS and its relevant members to enforce their signed Resolution, given that it specifically resolved to evict the illegal residents of the aforementioned compound. If LCAPSSS officials deliberately refuse to execute or enforce the Resolution, a complaint can be filed against them under the Local Government Code and/or the 2017 RACCS. 1 Section 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. - An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office on any of the following grounds: (c) Dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty; Page 2 of 3

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY RITY OF THE SECRETARY: N VICTOR R. LLAMAS Under retary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELIAJVRULLLS-LRALLD/lasm Page 3 of 3
